survey: A single western cowboy boot in side view, toe pointing right, floating against a radial orange background. Parts: (1) A tall shaft that leans a little back. Its top is open and scalloped, and you can see into it. An embossed leaf/flame motif is on the outer face. (2) A raised welt seam goes around the ankle where the shaft joins the foot. (3) The foot or vamp tapers to a squared, slightly pointed toe. (4) A dark brown sole runs the full length under the foot and sits flush with the upper. (5) A stacked block heel sits under the heel counter and slants forward, as a real riding heel does. Sole and heel would support the boot properly. (6) A gold spur sits at the back of the heel, above the heel block. A curved band (the heel band and shank) wraps around the heel counter. A star-shaped rowel is fixed to the end of the shank and points backward. The shaft, foot, sole and heel all join cleanly, and nothing passes through anything else. The boot could be worn and walked in.

errors.where: Gold spur, front end of the heel band on the side of the boot
errors.what: The spur arm wraps forward around the heel and then sinks into the side of the boot. It has no end button and no strap over the instep to hold it, so nothing clearly fastens the spur to the boot. The star rowel is also fused flat onto the end of the shank, with no fork or pin it could spin on. These are simplifications that look odd on a close look, but the spur still reads as a spur.

fix: Make the gold spur a U-shaped heel band that wraps around the back of the boot heel and ends in a small button on each side of the ankle. Add a thin leather spur strap from those buttons across the top of the instep. Mount the star rowel between the two prongs of a small fork at the end of the shank, on a visible pin so it could spin.
